Senior Frontend Engineer, Payments Experience
Kestrel Financial — Chicago, IL (hybrid, 4 days onsite)

About the role
Kestrel is a consumer fintech platform for small business banking. The Payments Experience team owns every screen a customer touches when moving money: transfers, scheduled payments, approvals, and the reconciliation views their bookkeepers live in.

We're looking for a Senior Frontend Engineer to lead the interface work as we rebuild the payments surface. This is a frontend-majority role — roughly 80% of your time will be in the client codebase.

What you'll do
Build and own complex, stateful React interfaces for payment flows where a mistake moves real money
Drive the design system forward in partnership with Design, including accessibility conformance to WCAG 2.2 AA
Own client-side performance: bundle budgets, render profiling, and Core Web Vitals against a strict SLA
Work directly with Product on rapid experimentation — we ship A/B tests weekly
Participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation; payments incidents are all-hands and the team carries the pager heavily during month-end close
Mentor two junior frontend engineers as an informal part of the role

Requirements
6+ years of frontend engineering with deep React expertise
Expert-level TypeScript, including complex generic types in a large shared codebase
Strong CSS and layout skills; you can build a data-dense table view that stays usable at 200% zoom
Experience with GraphQL clients and normalized cache management
Demonstrated ownership of design system or component library work
Experience in fintech, payments, or another regulated domain

Nice to have
Next.js and server-side rendering at scale
Experience with feature flagging and experimentation platforms
Some backend familiarity — you'll occasionally touch our Node BFF layer

How we work
Hybrid: 4 days per week in our Chicago office, non-negotiable for this role
Month-end and quarter-end close are our peak periods and the team works extended hours through them
Fast-moving, high-ownership culture with a strong bias toward shipping
